summary.assessment: The model is dependable only on a single-panel chart whose numbers are printed beside simple marks (B1: 12 of 12 bar labels exact); the other correct figure, C5, came from the engine's vector pie reader with zero model calls and says nothing about the model. Its most damaging habit is that it never declines: all five no-data figures (A1, A2, A4, A5, C2) came back as scatter or line panels with rows, two of them with invented numbers (A1 3.19-5.6 for icons, A4 eleven 'R-Peak' values of 1.0). On data charts it fails mainly through structure and coverage rather than gross misreading: multi-panel figures are merged, mis-boxed or cut off as 'not read', so five of ten data charts lose most of their values (B2 0/180 after a 600 s timeout, C3 0/264, B5 9/30, C1 6/12, C4 8/24), and it habitually repeats the category as the series name, which makes the automatic scorer report 0 matches where the numbers are in fact right (C1 panel 2, B5, C4). The values it does read from geometry are mostly within 2-5 % of the axis range (B4 centres, C1 panel 2, 9 of 9 B5 medians, 6 of 8 C4 medians), with occasional scatter of 7-15 % (C1 panel 1, two C4 boxes). Intervals and printed statistics are not trustworthy: A3 returns the printed upper CI cap as the point estimate, B4 returns four of five intervals as offsets around zero, and B3 ignores all 15 printed AUROC values. It can be trusted on single-panel bar charts with printed values, and not on diagrams, multi-panel figures, interval or box plots without a chart/non-chart gate and a check of the bounds.
